title: What townsfolk say about the world outside
by: Dev (local model), checked by the writing room

items.name: the sects
lines: Them sects, they say, are where folks go to seek the impossible. A fool's errand if you ask me.
I heard the sects in the hills are like secret gardens, full of mysteries and teachings that bend reality itself.
Some folks leave to join sects and never come back, not even to say goodbye. It's like the hills themselves take them in.
Sects are the place where the old gods and the new meet, where the paths of the old war still echo.
You can see the towers from a distance, like the fingers of giants pointing to the sky, beckoning the brave and the curious.

items.name: the towers
lines: Them towers been standing since before the war, and they'll be here when we're long gone.
Said I seen lights, dancing high up in them towers at night, but no one believes me, leastwise not those that don't know their ghosts from a flicker of flame.
They say the sects are full of secrets, but the towers, they're something else. They whisper in the wind and the stones weep to them.
Old folk say the towers hold the secrets to bending qi to our wills, but others, they think it's just wind and echo, stories and shadow.
Travelers come and go, but the towers stay, watching over us with eyes older than memory.

items.name: strange lights
lines: Seen them floatin' over the hills at night. Strange, ain't it?
They say the towers power them, but who knows what else might be out there?
I heard the lights are the souls of fallen warriors, comin' back to haunt the battlefield.
Old folk say it's the gods watchin' over us, but I reckon it's just the old Nanite stuff in the stone.
Them lights move like they know what's in your heart, and that's the spookiest part.

items.name: travellers
lines: They come from far, these travellers, carrying tales of lands beyond the mountains.
Mighty warriors and clever thieves, all with something to hide behind their smiles.
The old man at the inn says they're all looking for the same thing: power, glory, or just a warm bed for the night.
A young girl whispered to me that they brought strange lights with them, not from this world.
We in Eliet don't travel much, so we look at them with half-awe, half-suspicion.

items.name: the old war
lines: They say the war was worse than the coldest winter, with spirits and shadows warring on the mountain.
Back then, the towers were still new and the sects were like families, not fortresses.
I heard the old war was fought with magic and fire, but also with whispers and cold iron.
Those who lived through it won't talk about it unless they've had too much to drink.
The war brought the first refugees to Eliet; they say it was a time when the valley was haunted by the dead.
